subject.title: Bound historical public repository proof reuse after expiry

question: Should historical public-repository proofs remain usable for an explicit post-expiry grace interval during GitHub outages, and if so what interval and failure behavior are acceptable?
rationale: The proposed five-second value in the closed unmerged PR is a security and availability policy choice with no supplied maintainer approval.

options.title: Approve a bounded grace policy
options.body: Define a documented interval and require matching runtime, D1-query, and boundary-test behavior.

options.title: Fail closed at expiry
options.body: Disallow post-expiry historical reuse, accepting reduced cached availability when GitHub verification is unavailable.

options.title: Defer the fallback change
options.body: Keep the existing behavior until maintainers decide the intended authorization-versus-availability tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Approve a bounded grace policy
recommendation.body: Define a documented interval and require matching runtime, D1-query, and boundary-test behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied merged history places this contributor closest to the public-proof fallback surface.
